title: Prevention and Treatment of Maternal Stroke in Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
summary: This AHA scientific statement synthesizes stroke prevention and urgent management during pregnancy and postpartum. It emphasizes prompt management of severe maternal hypertension and that pregnancy should not delay evidence-based acute stroke assessment and treatment. CT, CT angiography and MRI without contrast are described as suitable rapid imaging options, with early vascular neurology and maternal-fetal-medicine involvement.
findings: Pregnancy should not delay evidence-based acute stroke evaluation and treatment.
CT, CT angiography and noncontrast MRI are suitable rapid maternal stroke imaging options.
Maternal stabilization takes precedence over delivery planning; stroke alone does not mandate immediate delivery.
comparator: Prior variable general-stroke and obstetric pathways; not a trial.
population: Pregnant and postpartum patients at risk for or presenting with stroke.
limitations: A scientific statement based partly on consensus, not a new randomized trial or uniformly graded treatment guideline. The official AHA summary and PubMed abstract, not the complete journal article, were reviewed.
intervention: Multidisciplinary scientific guidance on prevention, imaging, acute treatment and maternal stabilization.
whyItMatters: Activate combined stroke and obstetric assessment without postponing indicated brain or vascular imaging. Stabilize the mother and address severe hypertension; stroke alone does not mandate immediate delivery.
evidenceNotes: Official AHA hub/Top Things to Know and PubMed abstract PMID 41603019 DOI 10.1161/STR.0000000000000514 reviewed. Epub January 28, 2026; April is print issue. ACOG endorsement listing dated January 2026; journal full text not reviewed. No verified correction found in targeted checking.
primaryEndpoint: Guidance on maternal stroke rather than a randomized primary outcome.
guidelineStrength: Scientific statement with consensus suggestions; no uniform formal class/level established from reviewed sources.
